1. The combat system is abysmal. You level up your character to 35 and you will still find with a 90% hit chance that you are missing but your enemies will go right through your resistances like butter. A boss will inexplicably increase damage until they delete you, invulnerability or not.
2. The graphics.
3. Many of the "puzzles" require you to figure out how to level up spells and then return someplace later, with no real notes on where. It makes a heck of a lot of progress hit-or-miss and boring.
4. Final critique is that some quests are bugged or do not make it clear how to progress. If you are a completionist, don't expect to complete everything.
5. Bonus: It annoys the snot out of me when I have a 4-person party that gets blocked easily and cannot be plotted for long distances of travel with no indication on how far away I can move the cursor. QoL issues.

Вот я и осилил вторую часть второго ремейка знаменитой в узких кругах игры Exile. В детстве мы с друзьями вместе проходили первую часть, купленную на диске, и требующую кейгена, которого тогда было нигде не найти. Интернета у нас тогда еще тоже толком не было. Позднее, еще когда Jeff не начал публиковаться в стиме, да и стим тогда еще не был популярен, я начал покупать игры прямо у него на сайте...
Первую часть Exile мы с друзьями мучали долго, но ко второй и третьей никто из них так и не перешел. Для меня вторая из детства вспоминается как "проходная" и весьма короткая. Как же я ошибался...
Пройдя ремейк A:EftP, я сразу же приступил ко второй части, но.. не осилил её. Я всегда стараюсь играть в RPG на максимальной сложности, но было так сложно, что я забросил игру. Ссейчас я уже понял, что соваться к Slith-ам на том этапе было просто рано. 
Спустя почти 6 лет (подумать только, сколько времени-то пролетело!), я вновь вернулся к игре и на этот раз прошел её от корки до корки, получив все ачивки. Да, играть на максимальной сложности тяжело, приходится иногда смотреть подсказки и по группе, и по локациям, тем более, что не всегда все очевидно. Не помню, как было в A:EftP, но здесь в конце игры противники становятся настолько жирными, что даже на обычных врагов порой уходит немало времени. Все магии 3его уровня раскиданы по разным локациям, при этом некоторые низкоуровневные магии так размещены, что получить их можно лишь ближе к концу игры (например, Icy Rain). Кто-то может сказать, что это бесполезная магия, но это не так - это единственное заклинание у мага, которое можно запускать с большого расстояния и частично за стены и преграды, а на третьем уровне еще и дает шанс обездвиживания. Именно им я большую часть времени и бил последнего босса, который может ваншотнуть всю группу, независимо от прокачки и зелья неуязвимости. При этом в большинстве случаев, в отличие от первого ремейка, заклинания 3его уровня не являются жизненноважными, и нет проблемы выучить их сразу (в первом ремейке была проблема с тем, что выучив заклинание из книги, нельзя было получить 3ий уровень, т.к. выше 2го учителя в принципе не учили). 
Часто приходится бегать из данжа в данж. Не рассчитывайте, что сможете "зачистить" даже первые локации с первого раза - боссы часто значительно сильнее других врагов, некоторые места потребуют большего навыка Tool Use, знания Move Mountains и Dispel Barrier, причем порой 2 уровня, а иногда и выше. 

Подводя итоги, скажу, что игра отличная, спокойная. Не нужно ничего решать, делать выбор, бояться, что вы где-то что-то сделали не так (есть буквально пара моментов, где можно что-то испортить), просто творите добро и побеждайте зло. Нет никаких дилемм или сложных решений. При этом игра на максимальной сложности потребует уйму времени, за указанные 50 часов пройти не получится. 

Пара советов для начинающих играть на максимальной сложности: выбирайте группу из 4 человек, два из которых Жрецы, два - Маги. Сначала первый жрец качается в воина-танка (т.е. качает Melee+Hardiness до 8 уровня), а ближе к финалу уже активно качает Priest Spells и немного Mage Spells (минимум до 3его уровня, чтобы он мог пускать Haste в начале). 

P.S. С некоторым ужасом планирую перейти к ремейку третьей части. Очень отталкивает наличие временных рамок в ней, когда так спокойно уже не поисследуешь, т.к. города со временем рушатся, а персонажи погибают...

[b]TL; DR[/b] Return to Avernum, defend our underground home, save us from imperial tyranny! Try not to get radiation poisoning in the process.
Keep in mind that this is a remake of a remake, the original [i]Crystal Souls[/i] released in ’96. 

[b]Note[/b] You can play the [i]Avernum[/i] series in any order but if you do not play them in chronological order, you will miss out on the evolving circumstances, such as why we were justified in doing what we did. 
Since this is a sequel, you should expect some spoilers for the preceding game.

[h1] Story [/h1]
The Emperor was assassinated and they are blaming us! To arms to arms! The surface dwellers are invading Avernum!
Humans, Nephilim, and even Slithzerikai are fighting as one to protect their freedom but it is not enough, the Archmage Garzahd leads the invasion, we are pushed further and further back! Without assistance Avernum is doomed, but something remarkable happens, indestructible barriers are appearing, and paths into the deepest reaches of the underworld are revealed...

[i]Crystal Souls[/i] is a sequel, it takes place in much the same areas as [i]Escape from the Pit[/i] so it serves a nice chance to reunite with people and places you know. Sometimes you can finish what you started, finally cleansing the darkness with rituals of sanctification, others you can see the ruins of an old settlement or put acquaintances out of their misery. When a game takes place in the exact same place as its predecessor, this is how you do it, give us opportunities to see what has changed, and change things up so that it feels new and different, even when it is not. 
But fear not for there are other things in [i]Crystal Souls[/i], the narrative and the situation are focused on the imperial invasion, and as you explore you will find military installations, the massacre of Slithzerikai civilians, and mages up to no good. It manages to offer some variety in quests despite ostensibly being about a war, and as for Garzahd, he is an interesting character, learning about him, and speaking with him, is fun. 

However, the most interesting aspects of [i]Crystal Souls[/i] are the friendly faces of the Slithzerikai, the Nephilim, and their newfound alliance with the Avernites. There is tension between them, and even the ones who have joined the alliance might have some reservations about it, this can make for some interesting dynamics, and I love that both species are playable, even if the dialogue remains the same. However, there is something more important, histories of bloodshed and mutual distrust are interesting, but are they as interesting as the Crystal Souls themselves? 
The Vahnahtai were teased throughout [i]Escape from the Pit[/i], shimmering cloaks, strange corpses, and a language beyond your comprehension, now, far far below Avernum, they are awakened, and they are not pleased. They demand an envoy and promise certain doom if humanity does not comply. Well, I guess we are up.
It is hard to compare them to any other fantasy species because they might as well be aliens, they feel so different from anything you have ever seen that it is a treat to learn about them, their technology, beliefs, and the floating crystals of their forebearers.
They are also among the most relatable aliens I have ever met, because they, just like me, can sleep for centuries on end, they do it to prevent starvation, letting the outside world recover, and letting the mushroom fields replenish, but I do it on accident. 

[h1] Presentation [/h1]
Visually it is basically indistinguishable from [i]Escape from the Pit[/i], and it similarly inherits a lot of models from previous games such as [i]Geneforge[/i]. If you are looking for a series with more involved art, you are in the wrong place
[i]Crystal Souls[/i], has a title track, it is the only music you are getting, I would describe it as apprehensive, and tense. It almost loops in on itself which I chose to interpret as a conscious decision to mirror the stalemate that has settled in the underworld, because I think that sounds cool.

There are also a few handful art pieces, usually accompanying one of three primary quests you receive, and since they often relate to endings I will not say much. However, there is one with a trio plucking mushrooms in the cavern, and it looks very nice, peaceful, and calm, a reminder of the sort of people you are protecting. 

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
All Spiderweb Software games play the same sort of way, and the [i]Avernum[/i] series is no exception. [i]Avernum[/i] focuses on being a sort of sandbox dungeon crawler, you can explore an open world filled with events, towns, handcrafted dungeons and underground rivers to block your path. It is simple but very entertaining if you are into it.
I reused the preceding sentences from my [i]Escape from the Pit[/i] review, because there are no major changes, and for that reason I will not get into the combat or exploration at any great depth. 

Moving from [i]Crystal Souls[/i] to [i]Escape from the Pit[/i] there is only one major difference, and that is the narrative, combat is basically unchanged and large swathes of the map are the exact same. 
I found it enjoyable, sometimes chilling, to reexplore familiar areas and see how the people and places I know have fared under the Empire’s advance, the difference in context and concept makes [i]Crystal Souls[/i] feel completely different even when certain area maps are basically copied. That is not to say that [i]Crystal Souls[/i] does not contain new maps, far from it, there are a number of new locations, some of them are strongholds of the Empire and others are further below... 

I prefer [i]Crystal Souls[/i] over [i]Escape from the Pit[/i], and that was a very early realisation. This was partly due to the more focused introduction, you are not thrown into a vast world, instead you are given a closed area, and clear goals until you are strong enough to wander about freely.
Yet my preference is largely because of the set pieces, and the new locations in the land of the Vahnahtai, and as stated, reexploring familiar areas, discovering what has happened in the interim. So, I do recommend people to play this after they have played [i]Escape from the Pit[/i].
Tangents aside, it was the decent into the deeper reaches of the caves that really sold me on [i]Crystal Souls[/i], it is a fascinating section with fun areas and cool lore, and it happens at the very start of the game. It is also fairly challenging since it is an extended section without being able to return to town for free heals or new equipment, what you have is what you get, and you might not want to pick up those shimmering metals, I hear they poison you. 
Another great encounter is the Doomguard, for the ill-equipped it is one of the deadliest enemies in the entire game because they really do live up to their name. It is a sort of DPS-check, and it is the most fearsome tool in the empire’s arsenal. 

Unfortunately, the final quests were a bit of a let-down, in [i]Escape from the Pit[/i] they felt fulfilling and climactic, but in [i]Crystal Souls[/i] two of them are a bit underwhelming. They have a lot of narrative weight, and they do feel monumental from that perspective, but from a gameplay standpoint they are far less memorable than assassinating a sitting Emperor, at least the third quest is almost as good.

First off: I want to say that if you enjoy exploration, then you should prob get one of the Avernum games. Although I personally enjoyed Avernum 1 more, that was simply because Avernum 1 was my first Avernum game. However, if I were to start over, I'd probably just go straight for Avernum 2 as it has a more interesting story. Now onto the actual review:

It suffers all the issues from the first game, except this time I'm no longer really exploring as much as I'm trying to get through the story and answer some questions.

The good:

The introduction of the vahnatai is a really nice touch. Apart from the empire's invasion, the contact with the vahnatai and exploring their realm is the real backbone of Avernum 2's plot (it's even in the name!). Unfortunately, the first three chapters are basically rushed with a fourth chapter that drags on and on. 

The issues:
1.Your choices are pretty much inconsequential. 
2. Related to the first point -- NPCs are pretty 'dead' and similar to one another. Side quests are just distracting at this point. I mean come on -- if you tell me that there's an event 'later in the day', I expect that something will happen. 
3. I want to get on with the story (because that's the crux of the game), but I find myself having insufficient 'access rights' even after completing a bunch of inconsequential side quests. 
4. The combat is repetitive, amplified by all the pointless enemy encounters throughout the map. 
5. Verbose but meaningless writing and dialogues (same as in Avernum 1).

Overall, as with Avernum 1, the game plays more like a puzzle game than a story-driven RPG.

It would be great if someone can convince me otherwise. I really like the story, but I just can't drag myself through the repetitive combat and meaningless side quest just to 'unlock' the next segment of the story.

[h1] Бюрократия - их злейший враг.[/h1]

Avernum 2: Crystal Souls - прямое продолжение Avernum: Escape From the Pit. История продолжается спустя несколько лет после финала первой части. Злая Империя, заселившая огромную сеть подземных пещер под названием Авернум многочисленными своими противниками, перестала сюсюкаться с ними и организовала полномасштабное вторжение. Героев первой части уже давно никто не видел, так что под управление игрока попадает новая команда. После войны с другими расами, осевшими под землёй, большинство народов стали жить вместе. Однако помимо угрозы со стороны Империи, из глубин пещер поползли слухи о новом враге. 

Avernum 2: Crystal Souls - хорошее продолжение. Оно развивает идеи первой части и вводит новые вещи.

Во-первых, благодаря событиям первой части, теперь в команде игрока есть не только люди, но и представители двух других местных рас: нефелимы, которых в переводе ласково зовут "котята" и слиты. Обе расы со своими преимуществами и недостатками. Но на этой ролевой отыгрыш заканчивается. Классов персонажей по прежнему три: воин, жрец и маг. Да, можно сделать двух разных воинов - на ближний бой и на дальний, но дальше этого эксперименты не доходят. Различной экипировки тут море, но действенной - единицы. У моего воина, в конце игры, скопилось пара копий и четыре разных меча, которыми можно было жонглировать в зависимости от противников, а вот остальных члены партии ходили исключительно в персональных вещах. Прокачка тоже не особо претерпела изменений - довольно быстро я набил своим подопечным сперва двадцатые уровни, а спустя ещё десяток часов - тридцатые. После этого долгое время мои персонажи просто автоматически улучшали характеристики при получении новых уровней, а на 35м мой жрец вновь получил очки навыков, которые распределял я. 

Во-вторых, карта игрового мира тут вновь довольно огромна, да и обзавелась новыми пещерами. Однако тут, довольно неожиданно, игра стала ставить палки в колёса. Если в первой части, помимо инстинкта самосохранения, игрока исследовать пещеры притормаживала получаемая им репутация, то теперь ещё добавили аж пять уровней допуска. Два уровня - у авернитов и ещё три - у [spoiler] имперцев [/spoiler] . В принципе, первое ограничение можно понять - шпионов немало в пещерах. A Direct Sequel to the First Game.

From the starting conditions, it becomes clear that all potential main objectives of the first part were achieved. Avernum has attracted the attention of the Empire, and it invades the underground world to seek revenge. A war of annihilation begins. It becomes evident why all characters consider the Empire unbeatable. It knows no mercy and enslaves and destroys everything in its path – representatives of all races, and even dragons and demons!

Nephilim and Slithzerikai join forces with humans to fight the invaders together. The Avernites know the terrain better, so they manage to inflict significant damage on the enemy using ambushes and guerrilla tactics, but the enemy's resources are inexhaustible, and it slowly but surely pushes Avernum back. Meanwhile, a strange magical anomaly occurs – indestructible magical barriers block local caves, separating towns and disrupting communication between them.

The player controls a new party of four characters, new recruits in the Avernum army, who are tasked with fortifying the dungeon's border. These heroes are sent by the garrison command on a reconnaissance mission to find a breach in the barrier and establish contact with the King of Avernum. This leads to the establishment of contact with a third party, hints of whose existence were only encountered in the first part of the game. The Vahnatai people are different from anything familiar, and it is entirely unclear how they will react, as it is unknown how they think.

Gameplay and Innovations

The gameplay hasn't undergone significant changes; there are hardly any new features. The game uses the same strengths as its predecessor – an authentic world, atmosphere, and an engaging story. The action takes place mainly on the same map as the first game (i.e., the territory of Avernum), but now it has undergone significant changes due to the war – destroyed cities, collapsed caves, new outposts, etc.

In the first game, characters regarded the player's party as some kind of dubious adventurers, but here they are honored as elite soldiers protecting the oppressed people of Avernum from the Empire's wrath. In the first part, you could either be a hero or simply escape to the surface, but here, to "win," you will have to stop the Empire's invasion. The main objectives are: to facilitate an alliance between Avernum and the Vahnatai, destroy the Empire's portal through which reinforcements and supplies constantly descend into the dungeons, and eliminate the invasion's commander.

If previously you just followed your interests, here you are entrusted with the survival of entire peoples. This adds more epicness to all events.

I believe the game is a worthy continuation of the series. It retains all the best features of the first part and adds new elements that make the gameplay more exciting and rich.

Avernum 2: Crystal Souls is a strong step up on Escape from the Pit.

Don't get me wrong, it doesn't make sweeping changes. The graphics and sounds are exactly the same as in the previous game, the levelling system and balance are only slightly changed, and so on. 

Where Crystal Souls excels is in the storytelling, worldbuilding, and world design. 

Where Escape drops you into a fairly stable world and sends you out to adventure, Crystal Souls starts with turmoil - an invasion from the surface, and unexplained magical phenomena cutting off regions from one another. There's urgency and mystery.

Where Escape builds the exile-prison-caveworld of Avernum, Crystal Souls takes you deeper, into the land of the Vahnatai, a really interesting underground race. Avernum is still there, as vast as ever, but now there's this additional layer that breathes more life into the settting.

Where Escape gives you the appearance of freedom - but actually, due to the levelled world, requires you to stick to a vaguely-set path - Crystal Souls is a bit more guided of an experience. It's not until the third act that the game opens up the full world to you, and even there, there's challenges in unlocking more areas through acquiring boats, magical items, clearances, and passports. This was huge for me, as in Escape I often felt lost, stumbling around until I found level-appropriate content. Crystal Souls showed me a path, while still giving freedom - there's still three separate routes to beating the game.

If you like Spiderweb Software's style, this is their best game.
